sections.h2: Does Virginia have an estate or inheritance tax?
sections.html:
No. The state dropped both its estate tax and its inheritance tax. Receiving a house from a relative creates no Virginia death tax bill.

You may still hear otherwise because the rules changed. Until July 1, 2007, Virginia's estate tax was tied to the federal credit for state death taxes. Once Washington eliminated that credit, the Virginia tax went with it.

One narrow exception remains: certain remainder interests are still subject to the inheritance tax. Public Document 15-93 has a section on them. When the house moves through a life estate or a trust remainder, check with a probate attorney or the Department of Taxation first instead of assuming zero.

ChargeAmountWho it hits
Estate taxNone today; repealed in effect after July 1, 2007Heirs of any house
Inheritance taxNone, except certain remainder interestsHeirs of life estates or trust remainders
Probate tax10 cents per $100 of estate valueEstates over $15,000
Deed grantor tax50 cents per $500 of considerationWhoever signs the sale deed

Only two of these charges apply to a normal estate sale: the probate tax when the estate opens, and the deed tax when the house sells. Both are explained below.

The probate tax is charged when a will is probated or an administrator is appointed, and it follows the size of the estate, not the identity of the heirs.

Code 58.1-1712 sets the rate at 10 cents per $100 of value, with any leftover fraction of $100 counted. Estates of $15,000 or less are exempt. Section 58.1-1713, the next one, governs how value is determined.

For current steps and any filing fees, ask the circuit court clerk in the city or county where the person lived.

sections.h2: Order of events for an estate sale
sections.html:
The order is usually the same. First the will goes to probate at the circuit court. The named executor qualifies, or the court appoints an administrator when there is no will or no executor, and the probate tax comes due at that point. With the certificate of qualification in hand, the personal representative can list the house or take a cash offer.

Then the title company searches title, requests a payoff from the Treasurer, and confirms the signer's authority. Closing day brings the recorded deed and the grantor tax, paid through the clerk. Property tax and any mortgage come out of the proceeds, and the remainder belongs to the estate. A cash buyer shortens the middle stretch, since no lender underwriting or appraisal holds things up.

Heirs in other states can generally leave the signing to the personal representative.

Under Code 64.2-521, an executor may sell and convey real estate and collect the proceeds when the will directs a sale and leaves the job to no one else.

If no executor qualifies, or the ones who did die, resign, or are removed, an administrator with the will annexed holds that power too, unless the will clearly says otherwise.

Before listing, collect:

  • The will, plus the certificate naming the personal representative.
  • Any direction in the will to sell the real estate.
  • The deed, the newest tax bill, and the latest mortgage statement.
  • The title company's list of papers it needs from the clerk's office.

No state estate tax payment appears on that list. The title company can say which authority papers it wants.

sections.h2: Property tax still attached to the house
sections.html:
A death does not clear the property tax. It stays with the house and ranks first: Code 58.1-3340 puts the real estate tax lien ahead of every other lien or encumbrance until the taxing authority has been paid.

Penalties and interest count as taxes under that section, and sale proceeds must cover taxes and levies on the real estate first. The purchase agreement prorates the seller's share, so it should spell out who pays for which dates.

Localities set their own schedules, and Virginia Beach is one example. Its bills come due in two installments, December 5 and June 5. A late payment costs a 10% penalty or $10, whichever is greater, plus 9.6% yearly interest. Unpaid taxes can lead the city to record a lien at the Circuit Court clerk, and once delinquency reaches three years plus the current tax year the Treasurer can advertise the property and charge a $25 fee.

Inherited a house with back taxes? Get a payoff figure from the local Treasurer before you list. Closing pays it out of the proceeds.

The estate owes the grantor tax on the deed, as any seller would. Code 58.1-802 charges 50 cents per $500 of consideration, rounding up any fraction. The grantor pays it unless the contract shifts part or all of it to the buyer.

Recording requires the consideration on the deed's first page and the clerk's certification that the tax was paid. The clerk collects the money and divides it between the state and the locality.

Whether the estate or the buyer bears it follows the contract.

sections.h2: Federal tax on an inherited sale
sections.html:
No state death tax does not make the sale tax free, because the IRS can still tax a gain. An inherited house gets its basis under special rules in Publication 551, Basis of Assets, rather than from what the decedent paid. Publication 544 covers the holding-period exceptions for property from a decedent. Whether there is any gain turns on that basis and the final sale price.

  • Find out from the estate's preparer how basis was set.
  • The $250,000 and $500,000 home sale exclusion only helps if you owned the home and lived in it as your main residence for 24 of the last 5 years.
  • A Form 1099-S means the sale must be reported, even if the gain is excluded.
  • A loss on a home used personally cannot be deducted.

A separate page on this site explains how the federal rules interact with Virginia income tax on a house sale.

sections.h2: When an as-is cash sale helps an estate
sections.html:
Families wanting a certain closing date and no repair list often prefer it, particularly while holding costs mount. Taxes, insurance, utilities, and lawn care continue until closing, and a vacant house brings added risk.

Selling as-is ends the repair haggling, which helps when the heirs are scattered across states. A title company still handles closing, and the personal representative must still show authority to convey.

Questions about paperwork or timing are welcome. We do not give tax or legal advice, so let a probate attorney confirm who may sign.

faqs.q: Is there Virginia inheritance tax on a house I inherit?
faqs.a: No, with one narrow exception for certain remainder interests. A house that arrived through a life estate or trust remainder is worth a call to a probate attorney.

faqs.q: How much is the Virginia probate tax?
faqs.a: Code 58.1-1712 sets it at 10 cents per $100 of estate value. Estates of $15,000 or less owe nothing.

faqs.q: Does an executor need every heir to sign a sale?
faqs.a: Where the will directs a sale and names nobody else to handle it, Code 64.2-521 lets the executor sell and convey alone. Other wills vary, so an attorney should confirm.

faqs.q: Who covers unpaid property tax on an inherited house?
faqs.a: Closing pays it from the sale proceeds. Code 58.1-3340 ranks the tax lien first, and the contract prorates the seller's share.

faqs.q: Will I owe federal tax if I sell inherited property?
faqs.a: Maybe. Gain is taxable, and Publication 551 sets the basis rules for inherited homes. Many sales show little or no gain, but a tax professional should check.
